_comment: Mutation testing for the whole pure-TS domain (@oilio/shared) — utils, domain aggregates (reducers + replay), event-store, value objects, type validators. A surviving mutant = a behaviour no unit test pins. This package is where mutation pays off: pure logic, no Next/emulator, ~91% line coverage and a fast unit suite. The web is intentionally NOT mutated — its real net is the integration/e2e suite (Stryker reruns the unit suite per mutant; web unit coverage is ~14%, so mutating it would just yield no-coverage mutants).
_perf_comment: Tuned for the 1-vCPU saas-linux-small CI runner, where the job was timing out in the initial dry run (the full vitest config booted jsdom + the React setup + 98 non-domain test files: ~270s of `environment` startup per test-runner). Levers, by impact: (1) a dedicated `vitest.stryker.config.ts` runs ONLY the pure-domain suite under `environment: node` (env startup 273s -> 13ms locally); (2) `ignoreStatic` skips full-reload static mutants; (3) `incremental` re-tests only changed files on subsequent nightlies; (4) `concurrency` pinned to the runner's real CPU quota (1 vCPU -> 2 processes; oversubscribing thrashes). coverageAnalysis stays `perTest` (fastest mode).
_thresholds_comment: Whole-domain score (NOT cherry-picked) = 87.13% measured 2026-06-19 on the full 3524-mutant run (2264 killed / 230 survived / 4 timeout / 105 no-cov / 0 errors). This is UP from the ~77.4% pre-`ignoreStatic` plateau: `ignoreStatic: true` (added for CI perf) drops static mutants — the INITIAL_* / load-time-evaluated equivalents that no test could ever kill — from the DENOMINATOR. The rise is honest (the real surviving population is unchanged), not maquiagem. break = regression floor just below the measured score (85, ~2pp under 87.13 to absorb v8 run-to-run noise); ratchet UP as survivors are killed. Never set break above the real score to make it look good.
